verses.2: How long will you torment my soul, and how long will you heap up words against me?
verses.3: Know this only: it is God who has done this to me. You heap insults upon me, but you do not shame me.
verses.4: Even if I were to speak, my words would be foolish, and my thoughts would be scattered without purpose.
verses.5: But if I were to be guilty, you would magnify yourselves over me and heap disgrace upon me.
verses.6: Know this: it is God who has struck me, and His net is cast around me.
verses.7: I cry out in injustice, but no one answers. I call for help, but there is no justice.
verses.8: He has set a barrier around me, and I cannot pass through. He has cast darkness over my paths.
verses.9: He has stripped my honor away and taken the crown from my head.
verses.10: He has torn me apart on every side, and I wander. He has cut down my hope like a tree.
verses.11: His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
verses.12: All at once, His companions gather against me, and they set up their tents around my tent.
verses.13: My brothers have distanced themselves from me, and those who knew me now treat me as a stranger.
verses.14: My relatives have forgotten me, and those who were close to me have turned against me.
verses.15: My household and my servants now regard me as a foreigner. I am a stranger in their eyes.
verses.16: I called to my servants, but they did not answer. I begged them with my mouth, but they paid no heed.
verses.17: My breath was a stranger to my wife, and I treated my children with kindness.
verses.18: Even the children of my household despise me. When I rise, they speak against me.
verses.19: All my companions loathe me. Those I loved have turned against me.
verses.20: My flesh clings to my bones, and my skin clings to my bones.
verses.21: Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me.
verses.22: Why do you chase me like God? Why do you not grow weary of my flesh?
verses.23: Oh, that my words were written down, that they were inscribed in a book.
verses.24: That they were etched with an iron chisel and with lead in the rock forever!
verses.25: I know that my Redeemer lives, and that in the end He will rise upon the dust.
verses.26: And after my skin is destroyed, from my flesh I will see God.
verses.27: I myself will see Him, and my eyes will behold Him. I will no longer be a stranger, for my kidneys delight in Him.
verses.28: If you say, "What can we do to him? For his root has been found guilty,"
verses.29: then fear the sword, for wrath comes from the sword. Then you will know where your punishment lies.

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "My breath was a stranger to my wife" — the Hebrew is ambiguous; the phrase could mean that my breath was not recognized by my wife, or that my presence became strange to her. The former is taken here.
- v. 25: "Redeemer" — the Hebrew is גאל, which is rendered as "Redeemer" following the glossary.
- v. 27: "my kidneys delight in Him" — the Hebrew uses the plural "kidneys" (כליות) as a poetic or metaphorical term for deep affection.

[1] Then Job responded and said:
[2] How long will you torment my soul, and how long will you heap up words against me?
[3] Know this only: it is God who has done this to me. You heap insults upon me, but you do not shame me.
[4] Even if I were to speak, my words would be foolish, and my thoughts would be scattered without purpose.
[5] But if I were to be guilty, you would magnify yourselves over me and heap disgrace upon me.
[6] Know this: it is God who has struck me, and His net is cast around me.
[7] I cry out in injustice, but no one answers. I call for help, but there is no justice.
[8] He has set a barrier around me, and I cannot pass through. He has cast darkness over my paths.
[9] He has stripped my honor away and taken the crown from my head.
[10] He has torn me apart on every side, and I wander. He has cut down my hope like a tree.
[11] His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
[12] All at once, His companions gather against me, and they set up their tents around my tent.
[13] My brothers have distanced themselves from me, and those who knew me now treat me as a stranger.
[14] My relatives have forgotten me, and those who were close to me have turned against me.
[15] My household and my servants now regard me as a foreigner. I am a stranger in their eyes.
[16] I called to my servants, but they did not answer. I begged them with my mouth, but they paid no heed.
[17] My breath was a stranger to my wife, and I treated my children with kindness.
[18] Even the children of my household despise me. When I rise, they speak against me.
[19] All my companions loathe me. Those I loved have turned against me.
[20] My flesh clings to my bones, and my skin clings to my bones.
[21] Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me.
[22] Why do you chase me like God? Why do you not grow weary of my flesh?
[23] Oh, that my words were written down, that they were inscribed in a book.
[24] That they were etched with an iron chisel and with lead in the rock forever!
[25] I know that my Redeemer lives, and that in the end He will rise upon the dust.
[26] And after my skin is destroyed, from my flesh I will see God.
[27] I myself will see Him, and my eyes will behold Him. I will no longer be a stranger, for my kidneys delight in Him.
[28] If you say, "What can we do to him? For his root has been found guilty," 
[29] then fear the sword, for wrath comes from the sword. Then you will know where your punishment lies.
